people.name: Lisette Wallawalla (Tawasaqklie)
people.role: Narcisse Lavadour’s mother
people.note: Her birth name, the creator writes, was Tawasaqklie, “one who gets her work done early” in Walla Walla Sahaptin. Whether she was a daughter of Peopeomoxmox is a family tradition the creator records as undocumented and undisproved.
people.source: Zybach 2015, Douglas County Pioneer, September 2015, pp. 55–56; the creator’s section index, Appendix C.

people.name: Solomon Bigham
people.role: Mary Alice Bigham’s father
people.note: The creator writes that it is possible Martha and Solomon were married at some point, and asks openly who knows anything about him between 1864 and 1868.
people.source: Zybach 2015, Umpqua Trapper II, pp. 8 and 20.

people.name: Letitia Carson
people.role: The subject of the series
people.note: Born enslaved in Kentucky between 1814 and 1818; came over the Oregon Trail in 1845; sued Greenberry Smith twice and won both times; proved a homestead claim on South Myrtle Creek in 1868; died in February 1888 and was buried in the Stephens graveyard.
people.source: Zybach 2015, BlackPast entry, p. 2; Zybach 2014, Umpqua Trapper, pp. 4–10.

people.name: David Carson
people.role: Letitia Carson’s partner; the estate the suits were about
people.note: Born in County Antrim; came to America about 1818 with his brothers and sisters; held a farm and a town lot in Platte County, Missouri, and became a citizen in October 1844; claimed 640 acres in Soap Creek Valley in 1845, reduced to 320 in 1850; died in September 1852 after a short illness.
people.source: Zybach 2014, Umpqua Trapper, pp. 4 and 6.

people.name: Adam Andrew Jackson (“Jack”) Carson
people.role: Letitia and David Carson’s son
people.note: Born in Soap Creek Valley in 1849. He stayed on South Myrtle Creek when the Lavadour families moved to the reservation, took the land from his mother, never married, and was buried beside her in 1922.
people.source: Zybach 2014, Umpqua Trapper, pp. 6 and 10.

people.role: Letitia Carson’s eldest granddaughter
people.note: Born 26 November 1864, Martha’s daughter; married the younger Joseph Lavadour. The creator publishes a photograph of the two of them dated 1938, and notes that she kept her father’s surname until she married. When she died is not stated on any page in this series.

people.name: Peopeomoxmox
people.role: Walla Walla leader
people.note: Killed and his body mutilated by Oregon Territory militia on 7 December 1855. The creator records, without endorsing, a family tradition that Lisette Wallawalla was his daughter.
people.source: Zybach 2015, Douglas County Pioneer, September 2015, p. 55.

people.name: John Robinson
people.role: Administrator of the Missouri side of the estate
people.note: Administered David Carson’s Platte County land and made the settlements of 1853, 1855 and 1857.
people.source: Missouri probate transcriptions, pp. 1–3.

people.name: Greenberry Smith
people.role: Administrator of David Carson’s estate; defendant in both suits
people.note: Born in Virginia, raised in Indiana, farmed in Clay County, Missouri, and came west in 1845. Appointed administrator in November 1852; held that Letitia and the children were property and not heirs; lost to her twice.
people.source: Zybach 2014, Umpqua Trapper, pp. 6–7.
